title: Design Leadership, Hands-On in the Layer Underneath
subtitle: Systems, tooling and governance — and what a year inside them teaches you about AI and the craft

cv.note: Tailored for the Director of Product Design role

bio.short: I lead design functions, and I spent the last year hands-on in the layer underneath design — systems, tooling, governance. It is how you learn what AI is really doing to the craft, and where the opportunity in it is.
bio.long:
I lead design functions. At Ninox I ran design and, for four months, product as well: nine people across design, UX writing, product and data science, on the Senior Leadership Team.

The last year has gone into the layer underneath design rather than design itself. Systems, tooling, governance. Hands-on, on purpose.

That decision is the whole point. You do not find out what AI is actually doing to design work by reading about it. You find out by building in it — what changes in a designer's day, what quietly breaks, and where the opportunity is. Bibel TV has no in-house design team, so I own UI quality across iOS, Android, web and connected TV with nobody to delegate it to. The standard had to live in the system rather than in review.

So the design system ships as an API and one commit reaches every platform. WCAG contrast is checked inside the colour engine, and a theme cannot ship failing it. And the build itself refuses off-system work — six checks that run the same locally and in CI, two of them written against mistakes I watched an AI assistant make and could not catch by reading. Run over a library already cleaned twice, it found 32 values that had drifted.

That is the part I would bring to a domain like this one. Not an opinion about AI in the front end, but a year of having done it, and a clear view of what it costs designers and what it gives them back.
